Akimov disk function and quadratic phase curve of Enceladus fitted to Cassini VIMS spectra at 0.55 micrometres, used to light the globe.

references.evidence: Filacchione et al. (2022) eq. 3 writes I/F = D(i, e, g) F(lambda, g). Eq. 4 gives D as Akimov's disk function, with the photometric longitude and latitude of eqs. 5 and 6, and eq. 7 fits F with a second-degree polynomial a0 + a1 g + a2 g^2, g in degrees. Table 3 (Enceladus photometric parameters) gives at 549 nm a0 = 0.887595, a1 = -0.00197692 and a2 = -3.33943e-05; 0.55 micrometres is the wavelength at which the paper reports its albedos. The fitted ranges are the paper's data selection: incidence and emission up to 70 degrees and phase from 10 to 120 degrees. The record holds the polynomial at 120 degrees beyond that phase.
references.locator: Eqs. 3 to 7; Table 3, 549 nm row; Table 1 caption
